questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off the bike.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves to prevent a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves to prevent a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden movements when possible.
Handle your motorcycle roughly.
Use only your front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements when possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: If you are riding behind another vehicle at night, you can tell if there are bumps ahead by:

options.text: Listening for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Looking at the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead to see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle ahead to see the road at night. The vehicle's headlights may show the road better than your lights. If the taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots.
Are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from learning to use the front brake correctly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear half-fingered gloves.
Wear full-fingered gloves.
Not wear gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use the rear brake to control your speed through the U-turn.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: An oily strip runs down the center of a lane. What should you know about it?

options.text: You must avoid it at all times.
It usually has good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
You should only ride on it if you share the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually has good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough traction for safe riding when it is dry. When it rains, traction is reduced. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so motorcyclists can ride on either side of it while still staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving again.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means the same as a red light. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard in the road, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
Adjust your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers about your presence.
questions.explanation: To reduce danger and injury, alert other drivers to your presence by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to fit the situation. Change your lane position and direction if needed.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle to control it properly?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to support your body. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced when turning.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists must keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles in normal conditions. In bad weather or other poor conditions, use a larger following distance.

questions.question: When can a motorcyclist pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear road space.
By riding on the shoulder.
By riding on grass if the ground is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear road space.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is clear pavement at least eight feet wide to the right of the vehicle you are passing. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: In areas where dangers are present, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Keep the same speed.
Assume you will be safe.
Hold the clutch and both brake levers lightly to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the clutch and both brake levers lightly to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Hold the clutch and both brake levers lightly so you can react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to prevent a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals.
Use the correct lane position.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct lane position.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to make your motorcycle visible is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam both day and night whenever it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do with the front brake?

options.text: Use it only in emergencies.
Use it together with the rear brake.
Do not use it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Long pants
Gloves
A baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear like long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible when riding. A baseball cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
On the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between you and other traffic.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side nearest the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding to the far side may tempt them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:

options.text: Required.
Recommended but not required.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look far ahead on the road.
Avoid areas with heavy traffic.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Scan the road well ahead of your motorcycle. Watch for potential hazards and react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
Put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually safest.

questions.question: When should you shift gears in a curve?

options.text: Only if you can shift smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the curve.
It is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: Change gears before starting a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause a skid.
